findings.text: The first lines tell a newcomer what Athena is, what a study is, and that this page is one. The reader can say what they are looking at within three short paragraphs.
findings.source: Header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository."

findings.text: This URL is Athena's home page, but almost the whole page is about a different project, firstmate. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena gets one sentence on Athena and then many screens of firstmate internals.
findings.source: Title and h1: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: These are Athena's main selling points, but the page never shows them. The study only shows reading and citing, so the newcomer has to take the main features on trust.
findings.source: Header lede: "has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost"

findings.text: The page does say why it matters, and the claims section delivers on it: each claim links to exact file lines at a pinned commit. A reader can check this themselves.
findings.source: Header lede: "Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim"

findings.text: The next step is clear, and a link near the top jumps to it. But it lists no prerequisites, such as Rust, supported platforms, or the AI model accounts or keys that a system running 'one AI model' and 'a different one' would need. A newcomer can't tell what they're signing up for.
findings.source: Next steps: "Install Athena from a checkout of its repository: ./setup.sh" and "Try it with a one-line request: athena ask "add a changelog""

findings.text: 'Place', 'capacity' and 'exit 75' appear in the Start here walkthrough without being defined in 'Words used first'. They are defined only in the Glossary further down. The same goes for 'PR', 'worktree' and 'harness'.
findings.source: One piece of work, start to finish: "If every place of a declared capacity is held, the spawn exits 75 and the item stays queued."

findings.text: This definition is circular, and the page never defines 'wake'. The 'ship' entry is also weak: "A kind of task, named next to scouts."
findings.source: Glossary, stale wake: "A wake after which the agent inspects a worker that may have stopped, looped or gone quiet."

findings.text: Being upfront about the gap is good. But a key term in the merge rule stays undefined, and the same caveat is repeated in the Start here list, the t10 card and the Glossary.
findings.source: Words used first, in scope: "The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it."

findings.text: There's a lot of repetition. The firstmate description is given twice in a row. The yolo, green and red rules appear in Words used first, What firstmate is, the walkthrough, the failure list, three cards and the Glossary. This makes an already long page longer for a newcomer.
findings.source: Start here: "Firstmate is a tool that keeps a backlog of programming tasks and hands each one to a separate AI coding tool" followed by the first bullet repeating it

findings.text: Some card summaries run to five or more sentences of qualifications. That buries the one-line summary the section intro promises: "Each card opens with a one-line summary".
